message.content:
You are a READ-ONLY code reviewer. Do NOT modify any files. Review ONLY the change below for ONE angle: **Altitude** — is each change implemented at the right depth, not a fragile bandaid or a special case bolted onto shared infrastructure? Prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over special cases.

Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. The change transports two Andes CSRs (mcache_ctl 0x7CA, mmisc_ctl 0x7D0) across the QEMU->vsim hybrid handoff so the cycle engine resumes with caches enabled (crt0's `csrw mcache_ctl` runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transport vsim resumes caches-off and inflates the measured cycle count ~5x).

Read these to judge depth/consistency with how the codebase already transports CSRs:
- include/hybrid/state_abi.h (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl added next to fcsr; ALL fields in this struct are individually named — is per-CSR a field the right altitude, or should there be an "Andes CSR block"/array? Note other CSRs like mstatus/mepc are also individual fields, so per-field IS the established altitude.)
- qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c (drain by find_reg name + read_reg64 — same as every other CSR)
- verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp (write_csr_tolerant — same mechanism as mscratch/L24 CSRs)
- verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp (IMPORTANT: do the new CSRs need to be RE-READ at drain like mscratch/L24 are, or is restore-only correct? Compare to how mtvec is "restored but not re-drained" per the codebase docs. Read state_drain.hpp drain_with_passthrough to see which CSRs get re-read, and judge whether mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl being restore-only-without-re-drain is the right call or an inconsistency/gap.)

Specific altitude questions:
1. Is per-CSR-field the right altitude, or a special case? (Compare to the existing struct — likely consistent, confirm.)
2. Restore-only vs restore+re-drain+verify: is leaving mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl out of state_drain.hpp and state_diff (the --verify path) the correct altitude, or a half-implementation that will surprise someone? State which is right and why, referencing how mtvec / mip are handled (CLAUDE.md documents mtvec as "restored but not re-drained").
3. Does writing mcache_ctl mid-debug via the same tolerant path as ordinary CSRs sit at the right level, or does cache-enable need special handling?

Return a short findings list (file, line, summary, the deeper fix) OR confirm the change is at the right altitude and consistent with existing CSR-transport infrastructure. Verify every claim by reading the actual files — especially state_drain.hpp.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. 1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 2 (L11): vreg[] widened from 64 to 128 bytes per register, which
25	// shifts every field after it. Readers reject version-1 files loudly (all
26	// three consumers check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
27	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2u
28	
29	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 (1u << 0)
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP   (1u << 1)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V    (1u << 2)
32	
33	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
34	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
35	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
36	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
37	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
38	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
39	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
40	
41	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
42	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
43	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
44	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
45	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
46	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
47	
48	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
49	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
50	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
51	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
52	
53	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
54	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
55	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
56	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
57	  uint32_t magic;
58	  uint32_t version;
59	  uint32_t flags;
60	  uint32_t hart_id;
61	  uint64_t pc;
62	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
63	
64	  uint64_t gpr[32];
65	  uint64_t fpr[32];
66	
67	  uint64_t mstatus;
68	  uint64_t mepc;
69	  uint64_t mtvec;
70	  uint64_t mcause;
71	  uint64_t mtval;
72	  uint64_t mscratch;
73	  uint64_t medeleg;
74	  uint64_t mideleg;
75	  uint64_t mip;
76	  uint64_t mie;
77	  uint64_t mcycle;
78	  uint64_t minstret;
79	  uint64_t satp;
80	
81	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
82	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
83	
84	  uint64_t vstart;
85	  uint64_t vtype;
86	  uint64_t vl;
87	  uint64_t vlenb;
88	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
89	  uint64_t vxsat;
90	  uint64_t vxrm;
91	  uint64_t vcsr;
92	
93	  // F13: warmup-window snapshot of cycle/instret counters, captured K insns
94	  // after vsim entry. Drain-only metadata; ResumeDriver never restores them.
95	  // Both zero when --vsim-warmup-icount=0 or the workload exited inside the
96	  // warmup window. Consumes 16 bytes from the original 232-byte reserved tail.
97	  uint64_t mcycle_at_measure_start;
98	  uint64_t minstret_at_measure_start;
99	
100	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
101	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
102	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
103	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
104	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
105	  uint64_t fcsr;
106	
107	  // Andes machine setup CSRs that crt0 writes once at boot and the program
108	  // then runs under: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches, mmisc_ctl
109	  // (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. Drained by the plugin, restored by
110	  // ResumeDriver. Without these the cycle engine resumes at the ROI with
111	  // caches DISABLED (its reset default) because the enabling write happened
112	  // on the functional engine, which has no cache model -- inflating the
113	  // measured window severalfold. Old state files carry 0 here (reserved
114	  // bytes read back as zero), i.e. "leave at the hart's reset value", which
115	  // is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump. Restored tolerantly:
116	  // an engine without these custom CSRs mirrors the write as a no-op.
117	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
118	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
119	
120	  uint8_t  reserved[192];  // zero-initialise on write; 256 - 3*8 (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) - 2*8 (warmup) - 8 (fcsr) - 2*8 (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)
121	};
122	
123	#ifdef __cplusplus
124	}  // extern "C"
125	#endif
126	
127	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
128	
129	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
130

## Altitude review: mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl CSR transport

**Verdict: the change is at the right altitude and consistent with the existing CSR-transport infrastructure. No code-altitude fix needed. One optional documentation nit.**

I verified every claim by reading the producer, both consumers, the ABI, the verify path, and the tests.

### Q1 — per-CSR-field vs. an "Andes CSR block/array": per-field is correct, confirmed
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h:67-118` names every CSR individually (`mstatus`, `mepc`, `mtvec`, ..., `fcsr`). Two new `uint64_t mcache_ctl; uint64_t mmisc_ctl;` fields match that established altitude exactly. An array/block would be *inconsistent* with the whole struct and over-engineered for two CSRs. The offset static_asserts (`state_abi_check.h:69-82`) and the reserved-tail bookkeeping (256 − ... − 2*8) are maintained correctly, and `state_abi.test.cpp` locks the new offsets. Correct.

### Q2 — restore-only (no re-drain, no verify): this is the RIGHT call, not a half-implementation
The codebase has three tiers, and the new CSRs land in the same tier as `mtvec`:
- Full round-trip (restore + re-read + verify): `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), `fcsr` (L20).
- Restore + re-read, not verified: `mip` (timer bit diverges), `mcycle`/`minstret` (counters).
- **Restore-only, not re-read, not verified: `mtvec` (documented in CLAUDE.md as "restored but not re-drained"), `mstatus` in `drain_with_passthrough`, and now `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`.**

Leaving them out of `state_drain.hpp:80-134` (`drain_with_passthrough`) and out of `driver/state_diff.cpp` is correct because:
1. **Zero functional impact.** There is no QEMU2 leg; the drained output file's CSR fields are consumed only by `--verify` (`state_diff`), which doesn't compare these. Re-reading them would refresh data nobody reads.
2. **No false-positive risk, internally consistent.** Not-re-drained AND not-compared go together. Even if compared, `ref` (QEMU oracle) and `got` (vsim passthrough) both carry the same crt0 boot value, so no divergence — *provided the ROI doesn't write them*, which holds because these are boot-setup CSRs (crt0 writes once, program runs under them), unlike `mscratch`/trap CSRs that the ROI legitimately mutates.
3. **Matches the `mtvec` precedent**, so it's not a novel special case.

The stated L23/L24 principle is "ResumeDriver restores it ⇒ re-read it so an in-ROI write reaches the drained state." The new CSRs technically diverge from that wording, but the divergence is sound (boot-static + dead output). The author already encoded the decision *by omission*: the `fcsr` comment (`state_abi.h:100-105`) explicitly says "re-read by StateDrain"; the `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` comment (`state_abi.h:107-118`) deliberately stops at "restored by ResumeDriver."

Optional nit (documentation altitude only, not code): the omission is easy to miss. A future maintainer extending `StateDrain` will see every other restored CSR re-read and may wonder why these two aren't. One clause — e.g. "not re-read at drain: boot-static, and the drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg)" — in the `state_abi.h:107-118` comment would make it as explicit as the `mtvec` exception is in CLAUDE.md. No need to actually add the re-drain.

### Q3 — cache-enable via the same tolerant path: right level, no special handling needed
`resume_driver.hpp:240-241` uses `write_csr_tolerant`, identical to `mscratch`/`mtvec`/L24 (`write_64bit_register` + `clear_cmderr_if_set`, `resume_driver.hpp:293-297`). This is correct because:
- Enabling caches is just setting a config bit while the hart is halted; it takes effect on `dret`/resume. No flush/invalidate semantics are invoked (those would be a distinct operation), so it is an ordinary CSR write.
- "Tolerant" is exactly right: a non-Andes engine lacks 0x7CA/0x7D0, so the write no-ops via the sticky-cmderr clear — same as the FPR/PMP tolerant writes.
- Ordering (after L24, before `mcycle`/`minstret`) is irrelevant: all writes happen halted and take effect together on resume.
- The "drained 0 ⇒ caches-off reset" claim is backed by `read_reg64` returning 0 on a NULL handle (`hybrid_handoff.c:264`), confirmed.

The plugin drain (`hybrid_handoff.c:233-234` resolve, `389-391` read) is byte-for-byte the same `find_reg`/`read_reg64` pattern as every other CSR. Tests cover both the wire offsets and the resume DATA0/DATA1 + write-command shape (`resume_driver.test.cpp` new case).

Net: implementation depth is correct on all three axes; the only thing I'd consider is the one-line rationale comment, and even that is optional.
